expect.arrive: South Entrance is a simple gate check, then a two-lane forested road; Grant Village and West Thumb both have proper paved lots that rarely fill this early.
expect.parking: Grant Village Visitor Center and West Thumb Geyser Basin both have full-size paved lots; neither is reported to fill before mid-morning.

paths.do: Roadside look at Moose Falls and Lewis Falls from the pull-offs, no stop at Grant Village.
Same pull-offs, plus the West Thumb Geyser Basin boardwalk loops on the lakeshore.
Both waterfalls, Lewis Lake picnic area, Grant Village Visitor Center, and the full West Thumb boardwalk.

trail.from: West Thumb Geyser Basin parking lot

expect.arrive: Old Faithful's lot is enormous but this is the park's single busiest stop; it fills on clear late-September mornings by mid-morning and overflows to a second lot across the road. The geyser itself is visible from the visitor center deck and much of the boardwalk without walking far, but the wider Upper Geyser Basin (Morning Glory Pool, Geyser Hill) needs real boardwalk time.
expect.parking: Main Old Faithful lot holds hundreds of cars but fills by mid-morning in good weather; an overflow lot sits across the road near the Old Faithful Inn.

paths.do: Check the prediction board at the Visitor Education Center, watch the eruption from the boardwalk benches nearby.
After the eruption, walk the boardwalk loop around Geyser Hill's smaller geysers and pools.
Boardwalk out toward Morning Glory Pool and back, past Castle, Grand, and Riverside Geysers.

d04s2.seasonal: Biscuit Basin, a short drive north of Old Faithful on the way to Midway, has been closed since a July 23, 2024 hydrothermal explosion and was hit by a second explosion on July 13, 2026; it remains closed indefinitely as of 2026 (nps.gov/yell/planyourvisit/conditions.htm). It is not on this itinerary but travelers sometimes expect to stop there — do not plan a stop.

expect.arrive: Grand Prismatic itself is a flat boardwalk loop right off the Midway Geyser Basin lot, but the spring's full rainbow color only reads from above; the classic overhead photo requires the separate Fairy Falls Trailhead lot one mile south, which is small and known to fill by mid-morning.
expect.parking: Midway Geyser Basin's lot is mid-sized and fills by late morning; the Fairy Falls Trailhead lot for the overlook is much smaller and fills faster — arrive before 10am or expect roadside parking.

paths.do: Walk the flat Midway boardwalk past Excelsior Geyser and along the edge of Grand Prismatic.
Drive to the separate Fairy Falls Trailhead and walk up to the Grand Prismatic Overlook for the postcard view from above.

paths.opt: Full loop with Firehole Lake Drive
paths.do: Midway boardwalk, the overlook hike, and the one-way Firehole Lake Drive past Great Fountain Geyser plus Fountain Paint Pots.

alt: Great Fountain Geyser Firehole Lake Drive

trail.from: Fairy Falls Trailhead, 1 mi south of Midway Geyser Basin

expect.arrive: Canyon Village has the biggest lots on this stretch and rarely fills; the individual overlooks (Inspiration Point, Artist Point) are small paved pull-offs a short walk from their own car parks, not from Canyon Village itself. The canyon and both falls are visible without much walking, but the best angles need the short paved paths at each overlook.
expect.parking: Canyon Visitor Education Center has a large lot; Artist Point and Inspiration Point each have their own smaller lots that fill on clear afternoons.

paths.do: Artist Point and Inspiration Point only, both short walks from their own lots.

paths.opt: Add Brink of the Lower Falls
paths.do: Same two overlooks plus the steep short trail down to the brink of the Lower Falls.
Both overlooks, Brink of the Lower Falls, Upper Falls View, plus Sulphur Caldron and Mud Volcano on the way south.

alt: Grand Canyon of the Yellowstone Lower Falls

expect.arrive: Gibbon Falls and Beryl Spring are both direct roadside pull-offs, no real walk. Norris has the biggest lot on this stretch and is the hottest, most acidic basin in the park; it's split into two separate boardwalk loops (Porcelain Basin and Back Basin) that don't connect at both ends, so plan which one(s) you're doing before setting off from the car.
expect.parking: Norris Geyser Basin's lot is large and generally has room outside of midday peak; Gibbon Falls and Beryl Spring are small pull-offs with a handful of spaces each.

paths.do: Gibbon Falls and Beryl Spring from the pull-offs, skip Norris's basins.
Same pull-offs, plus the shorter Porcelain Basin loop at Norris.
Porcelain Basin and Back Basin, the full Norris visit.

alt: Artists Paint Pots mud pots Yellowstone
d05s1.seasonal: Monument Geyser Basin's trail is a steep 2.4 mi (3.8 km) round trip climbing roughly 800 ft — real hiking, not a stroll (nps.gov/places/000/monument-geyser-basin-trailhead.htm and USGS). Given the no-strenuous-hikes rule, skip it and view the basin's steam plumes from the road instead.

trail.from: Norris Geyser Basin parking lot / Norris Museum
trail.caveat: Porcelain Basin and Back Basin are two separate loops, not one trail

expect.arrive: Roaring Mountain is a roadside pull-off with the steaming hillside visible straight from the car. Mammoth's terraces sprawl across a hillside above the village; the Lower Terraces have a boardwalk right off the main lot, the Upper Terraces are reached by a one-way drive loop above them.
expect.parking: Roaring Mountain's pull-off is small; Mammoth has several lots around the village and near the Lower Terraces, generally with room outside of midday.

paths.opt: Roadside and Lower Terraces boardwalk only
paths.do: Roaring Mountain from the pull-off, then the flat lower boardwalk loop at Mammoth.
Same, plus the one-way scenic drive above the terraces with its own pull-offs.

expect.arrive: Lamar Valley's turnouts are wide gravel shoulders right on the road, wildlife visible with the naked eye from the car in many cases. Mount Washburn's trailhead at Dunraven Pass is a real mountain summit hike — this is not a stroll, and the road itself sits at high elevation where a September storm can close it with little warning.
expect.parking: Lamar Valley turnouts are informal gravel pull-offs, plentiful but the best wildlife-viewing spots fill at dawn and dusk; Dunraven Pass trailhead lot is small and can fill on clear days.

paths.opt: Lamar Valley only, drive past Washburn
paths.do: Stop at the wildlife turnouts, continue over Dunraven Pass without stopping.
Same, plus a few minutes at the Dunraven Pass trailhead pull-off for the view without hiking.
The full out-and-back to the fire lookout summit — not recommended for this trip; strenuous, high elevation, real time cost.

d05s3.seasonal: The road over Dunraven Pass (Canyon to Tower) is scheduled to stay open through late September into October 2026, but it's one of the first roads to close if an early storm hits — check current conditions the morning of. The NPS also flags grizzly bears actively feeding on whitebark pine nuts on Mount Washburn in fall and recommends hiking only in groups of 3+ with bear spray — one more reason the drive-by option fits this trip better than the hike (nps.gov/thingstodo/yell-trail-dunraven-pass-mount-washburn.htm).

expect.arrive: This is the long transit leg — nine hours of driving from Canyon Village to West Glacier. Bozeman is a normal college-town downtown with metered street parking; Butte's Berkeley Pit has its own small paid viewing-stand lot right at the edge of the flooded pit.
expect.parking: Bozeman downtown has metered spaces and a few public garages; the Berkeley Pit lot in Butte is small but rarely full given the short visit duration.

paths.do: Gas and bathroom stops only, no detours.
Add a 30-45 minute walk through downtown Bozeman for dinner or coffee.
Same Bozeman stop, plus 20-30 minutes at the Berkeley Pit overlook in Butte.

alt: Berkeley Pit Butte Montana flooded mine
